definition: The promoter based genetic algorithm (PBGA) is a genetic algorithm for neuroevolution developed by F.
details: Bellas and R.J. Duro in the Integrated Group for Engineering Research (GII) at the University of Coruña, in Spain. It evolves variable size feedforward artificial neural networks (ANN) that are encoded into sequences of genes for constructing a basic ANN unit. Each of these blocks is preceded by a gene promoter acting as an on/off switch that determines if that particular unit will be expressed or not.

explainer.lead: A genetic algorithm that evolves neural networks of variable size by switching individual building blocks on or off. It matters because it lets network structure grow and shrink during evolution instead of being fixed in advance.

tiers.eli5: Think of each little piece of the network as a light with its own switch; evolution flips switches on or off, so the machine changes how many parts it uses.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to search over both weights and network topology at once, encoding each basic ANN unit as a gene preceded by an on/off promoter. A pitfall is that promoter control adds search dimensions, so the space of possible expressed networks is large.
tiers.paperLevel: Each basic ANN unit is encoded as a gene block preceded by a promoter gene acting as an on/off switch; only expressed units form the feedforward network. Networks are variable size, so the encoding is not a fixed-length vector.

explainer.example: A population member carries ten unit genes; its promoters express only six, so the decoded feedforward network has six units rather than ten.
